question:
(i) Explain why diffraction is more pronounced for light of larger wavelength.
(ii) A photon of light has wavelength $400\,\text{nm}$. Calculate its energy. Take $h=6.63\times10^{-34}\,\text{J s}$ and $c=3\times10^8\,\text{m s}^{-1}$. Also state how photon energy changes when wavelength decreases.

options.A:
(i) Diffraction is more pronounced for shorter wavelength light.
(ii) $E=\dfrac{hc}{\lambda}=4.97\times10^{-20}\,\text{J}$, and energy decreases when wavelength decreases.
options.B:
(i) Diffraction does not depend on wavelength.
(ii) $E=h\lambda=7.96\times10^{-32}\,\text{J}$.
options.C:
(i) For the same aperture, larger wavelength gives greater spreading, so diffraction is more pronounced for larger wavelength light.
(ii) $E=\dfrac{hc}{\lambda}=\dfrac{6.63\times10^{-34}\times3\times10^8}{400\times10^{-9}}=4.97\times10^{-19}\,\text{J}$. Since $E\propto\dfrac{1}{\lambda}$, energy increases when wavelength decreases.
options.D:
(i) Red light diffracts less than violet because it has longer wavelength.
(ii) Photon energy is independent of wavelength.
